# Increment

> Increment is an open-source Python library for A/B test analysis. It helps teams measure the impact of product changes using dataframes or SQL warehouses, with reusable metric definitions, effect estimates, uncertainty intervals, and shareable reports.

Analyze randomized experiments from dataframes or SQL warehouses, or
observational treatments from dataframes or warehouse definitions. Increment supports CUPED, power
analysis, MDE, sequential and always-valid inference, SRM diagnostics, IPTW,
DML, AIPW, encouragement designs, and heterogeneous treatment effects.

It does not assign traffic, manage feature flags, ingest events, or maintain a
separate event store.

## Documentation

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylejcaron/increment/main/README.md): Project overview and installation.
- [Quickstart](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/quickstart/): Analyze A/B tests from Python dataframes.
- [Reading results](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/reading-results/): Interpret effects, uncertainty, missing evidence and the experiment decision.
- [Result fields](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/result-fields/): Exact result fields, confidence sets, unavailable reasons and export behavior.
- [Method selection](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/choose-a-method/): Choose a design and estimator from the treatment process and analysis goal.
- [Data model](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/data-model/): Declare warehouse sources, exposures, metrics, and experiments.
- [Warehouse definitions](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/warehouse-definitions/): YAML fields, normalized joins, clustering and backend behavior.
- [Experiment specifications](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/experiment-specifications/): Declare views, run an analysis and save or reopen its results.
- [Saved data and replay](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/artifacts-and-replay/): Artifact publication, recovery, reader identity and replay contracts.
- [Saved formats](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/saved-formats/): Readable versions, refusal codes and migration routes.
- [Observational causal inference](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/observational/): Use IPTW, DML, and AIPW with explicit causal assumptions.
- [CUPED](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/cuped/): Reduce variance with pre-treatment data.
- [Variance reduction](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/variance-reduction/): CUPED formulas, source contracts, missingness and sequential restrictions.
- [Priors and Bayesian decisions](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/priors-and-decisions/): Declare relative-lift beliefs and interpret posterior probabilities separately from sampling inference.
- [Bayesian results](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/bayesian-results/): Prior scales, historical predictions, approximation, availability and saved posterior state.
- [Sequential registration](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/sequential-contracts/): Sampling assumptions, capture, continuation and checkpoint formats.
- [Family inference](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/family-inference/): Multiplicity membership, error allocation, selection and stored-run contracts.
- [Causal methods](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/causal-methods/): Observational adjustment, encouragement and logged-policy assumptions and calculations.
- [Switchback inference](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/switchback-inference/): Assignment laws, independent replicate grain, carryover and qualified inference.
- [Sitewide calculation](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/sitewide-calculation/): Observed-window rollout calculations, completeness, population and artifact examples.
- [Dashboard output](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/dashboard-output/): Static versus live reports, capture identity, confidence-set display and export contracts.
- [Validation evidence](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/validation-evidence/): Method assumptions, frozen comparisons, calibration scope and reproducible evidence records.
- [Release history](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/release-history/): Archived development changes; current compatibility and migration guidance remains in the API reference.
- [Power analysis](https://getincrement.io/docs/guides/power-analysis/): Calculate sample size, power, and MDE.
- [Planning methods](https://getincrement.io/docs/reference/planning-methods/): Solver inputs, numerical qualifications, missing answers and planning approximations.
- [API reference](https://getincrement.io/docs/api/): Public Python API.
